question: Should OpenClaw adopt ordered, first-owner configuration layers as its permanent opt-in managed-configuration authority model?
rationale: The design is technically credible, but accepting new configuration precedence, policy-tightening exceptions, and runtime immutability is a lasting product and security-contract decision that the RFC lifecycle reserves for maintainers.

options.title: Approve V1 Direction
options.body: Accept the narrow startup-only model and coordinate this RFC's acceptance with the linked implementation.

options.title: Revise Authority Model
options.body: Keep the draft open while owners change path ownership, monotonic exceptions, conflict handling, or runtime immutability semantics.

options.title: Decline Core Support
options.body: Close the proposal and retain managed overlay composition in Lobster or other hosting layers.

recommendation.title: Approve V1 Direction
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow startup-only model and coordinate this RFC's acceptance with the linked implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository governance identifies steipete as the final product decision owner, making this the strongest available routing choice for RFC acceptance.
